verdict: A regular fast food beef burger is lighter, an estimated ~300 kcal compared to a stall chicken burger with egg at ~500 kcal. The stall burger is higher in protein, but its calories and fat are also much higher.
why: A regular fast food beef burger is an estimated ~300 kcal, a stall chicken burger with egg ~500 kcal. About a 200 kcal difference.
The stall burger has 22 g protein, the fast food burger 15 g. The egg and chicken patty add the protein.
The stall burger has 26 g fat, more than double the fast food burger (12 g). Mayonnaise, margarine and oil on the griddle contribute a lot.
Regular fast food burgers usually come as a set with fries and a fizzy drink. The full set can end up higher than the stall burger.
when_a: A stall chicken burger is okay as a full dinner, not as a snack. Its protein helps keep you full until bedtime.
when_b: A fast food beef burger suits you when you need a quick meal. Order just the burger, not a large set.
tip: At the stall, ask for 'kurang mayo, kurang sos' (less mayo, less sauce) and add lettuce or cucumber. At fast food places, have the burger with plain water or plain tea.

faq.q: Is a stall burger without egg better?
faq.a: Calories drop a little, but you also lose protein. It's more effective to cut down the mayonnaise, sauce and margarine on the bun.

faq.q: What if I order a fast food set?
faq.a: Change the fries to a small size or share them, and choose a sugar-free drink. That's an easy way to save a few hundred calories.
